{{Quote|This is my personal battle cruiser&hellip;and I did not name it the ''Executor'' for nothing!|Darth Vader|<ref name="Doom Mission" />}}
The [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] '''''Executor''''' was the personal [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], the premier [[Command ship/Legends|command ship]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], and the first of the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] line. Designed by [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] [[Lira Wessex/Legends|Lira Wessex]] as a successor to the original [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]], the ''Executor'', at a monumental 19,000 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length, represented the largest traditional [[Warship/Legends|warship]] [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] had ever seen by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of its completion. The ''Executor'' bristled with more than 5,000 weapon emplacements, enough firepower to [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|blast]] any [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] surface to slag in [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]], and a military complement capable of annihilating any ground installation. The ''Executor''{{'s}} presence alone, however, was enough to frighten an entire [[Star system/Legends|star system]] into submission.

Construction on the ''Executor'' began under complete secrecy in the secluded [[Scarl system/Legends|Scarl system]], where Vader raised and trained [[Galen Marek]], his secret [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] apprentice, in a failed plan to overthrow [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] as galactic ruler. By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], the ''Executor'' was transferred to the [[Fondor Shipyards/Legends|Starship Yards of Fondor]] for the final stages of construction, under the overall direction of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Amise Griff]]. At [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]], the ''Executor'' became the failed target of internal [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotage]] by a group of traitorous [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] admirals, who hoped to destroy Vader's project to prevent their own decline in power. Once completed, the ''Executor'' made for [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], site of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Great Temple/Legends|base]]. Vader hoped to crush the Rebellion once and for all with his new weapon, but the ''Executor'' failed to stop the Rebel [[Evacuation of Yavin|evacuation from Yavin]], and Griff [[Death/Legends|died]] in the process.

For three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after Yavin, under the command of Admiral [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]], the ''Executor'' led Vader's [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]], the [[Death Squadron/Legends|Imperial Death Squadron]], in the Empire's hunt for the Rebellion's secret [[Alliance High Command/Legends|headquarters]] as part of Vader's personal mission to locate his son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the ''Executor'' led the Imperial victory at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], but due to the tactical blundering of Ozzel, Skywalker and the Rebellion leadership escaped, and Vader executed Ozzel for his failure. The ''Executor''{{'s}} admiralty immediately passed to [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]], under whom the ''Executor'' chased the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] from [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] to [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] in continued pursuit of Skywalker. The ''Executor'' again failed to capture Skywalker at Bespin, however, and so Vader's search for his son continued.

For a time, with the search for Skywalker on hold, the ''Executor'' returned with Vader to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where, in 3.5 ABY, tensions between Vader and [[Dark Prince|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] crime syndicate came to a head. In [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] above the Imperial [[Capital/Legends|capital]], the ''Executor'' [[Battle over Coruscant|obliterated]] Xizor's [[Falleen's Fist|personal skyhook]], killing Vader's nemesis and ending Black Sun's threatening influence on the Empire. Immediately afterward, the ''Executor'' was assigned to protect the construction site of the incomplete [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] in the remote [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]].

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the ''Executor''{{'s}} relatively short life came to a crashing end above the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]]. During the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the ''Executor'' led a massive Star Destroyer armada in trapping the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Fleet]] between itself and the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. However, the Rebels turned the tables on the Empire by attacking the ''Executor'' at point-blank range. A concentrated assault on the ''Executor'' at the climax of the battle brought down the massive Super Star Destroyer's [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], before a wayward [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|A-wing starfighter]], [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] by [[Arvel Crynyd/Legends|Arvel Crynyd]], crashed into the ''Executor''{{'s}} command bridge. With navigation failing, the ''Executor'' was sucked into the [[Gravity well/Legends|gravity well]] of the Death Star and collided with the battlestation, disintegrating on impact.

==Description==
===Design===
{{Quote|I&mdash;it looks like a battle cruiser, sir&hellip;the largest one I've ever seen!&hellip;''"<br />"''&hellip;The biggest thing this side of the Death Star, Threepio&hellip;|C-3PO and Luke Skywalker, upon first sighting the ''Executor''|<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes">"[[Darth Vader Strikes]]"</ref>}}
The ''Executor'' was the first of the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] line<ref name="SSDDatabank" /> and the premier [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].<ref name="GG3" /> Measuring a colossal 19,000 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] long, the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] marked a crowning achievement in [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineering]] for both the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] Navy and [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], the [[Warship/Legends|warship's]] designer.<ref name="SSDDatabank" /> Nearly twelve times as long as the 1,600-meter-long [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]],<ref name="SWCL" /><ref name="Star Destroyer Databank">{{DB|starship|imperialstardestroyer|Imperial Star Destroyer}}</ref> the ''Executor'' represented the largest traditional starship ever constructed by the Imperial Navy at the [[Time/Legends|time]] of its completion&mdash;only the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] and select [[Torpedo Sphere/Legends|Torpedo Spheres]] were larger.<ref name="EGVV" />

[[File:ExecutorEscort-BTMF27.png|thumb|left|265px|The ''Executor'', under escort by two decidedly smaller ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]]
Following the same recognizable [[Dagger/Legends|dagger]]-shaped design of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]], the ''Executor''{{'s}} superstructure resembled an arrowhead from above.<ref name="SSDDatabank" /> A smooth [[Titanium/Legends|titanium]]-reinforced [[Alusteel/Legends|alusteel]] hull<ref name="BTM" /> surrounded a massive island of habitable volume in the center of the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]],<ref name="SSDDatabank" /> which accommodated the command, control, operation, and habitat decks.<ref name="FactFile47" /> In the blackness of [[Realspace/Legends|space]], the ''Executor''{{'s}} interior lighting enshrouded the warship in a cerulean glow,<ref name="ESB" /> though the ''Executor''{{'s}} exterior was in fact a grayish hue,<ref name="NEC" /> darker than the traditional "[[Star Destroyer White]]" typical of the ''Imperial''-class line.<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref>

Rising above the dorsal technoscape of the ''Executor'', supported by a thick axis, stood the 285-meter-wide trapezoidal command tower&mdash;a veritable ship unto itself. In a true testament of the [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]] Drive Yards' design philosophy of "terror styling," the command tower was deliberately positioned in prominent view of any vessel bold enough to dare an attack. The command tower housed several key components of the Star Dreadnought,<ref name="SWCL" /> including the dual geodesic KDY [[ISD-72x deflector shield generator dome]]s<ref name="FactFile43" />&mdash;an enlarged version specially developed from those aboard ''Imperial''-class [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]]<ref name="CSWE-ISD-72x" />&mdash;which doubled as communications [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] globes; as well as the [[Imperial officer/Legends|officers']] quarters;<ref name="SWCL" /> [[Navigation computer/Legends|naviation computer]];<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook, Second Edition" /> briefing rooms; [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]] for the ''Executor''{{'s}} upper-echelon commanders; and, most importantly, the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]].<ref name="SWCL" />

In accordance with the ''Executor''{{'s}} standard command tower module found on many KDY-constructed warship classes, the bridge design mirrored that of the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer. A gleaming command walkway, separating twin crewman pits, led to a series of two-meter-tall [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] [[Viewport/Legends|viewports]] that offered an unobstructed view of space beyond. Although the command tower stood arrogantly exposed above the ''Executor''{{'s}} superstructure, the ship's [[Deflector shield/Legends|shielding]] system, which matched the power output of a medium [[Star/Legends|star]], kept it sufficiently protected from attack, making such Imperial pretentiousness a possibility.<ref name="SWCL" /> The ''Executor''{{'s}} shielding system was among the most powerful ever conceived for a warship.<ref name="FactFile43" />

The underside of the ''Executor'' contained the engineering sections;<ref name="SSDDatabank" /> the enormous primary [[Hangar/Legends|hangar bay]], which was large enough to dock an Imperial Star Destroyer<ref name="Official Figurine Collection 1">[[Star Wars: The Official Figurine Collection 1|''Star Wars: The Official Figurine Collection'' 1]]</ref> and thousands of [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]];<ref name="SOTG2007" /> and countless secondary docking bays and staging areas<ref name="GG5">[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi'', Second Edition]]</ref> located near the bow of the ship.<ref name="EGVV" /> Thirteen immensely powerful, [[Blood/Legends|blood]] [[Color/Legends|red]]-glowing<ref name="SSDDatabank" /> KDY [[Executor-50.x engine/Legends|Executor-50.x]] [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight drive]] [[Engine/Legends|engine]] thrusters<ref name="Ships of the Fleet" /> propelled the warship forward at a maximum speed of 1,230 G,<ref name="NEGVV" /> or forty [[megalight]]s.<ref name="BTM" /> The thruster exhaust bells created an energy wash so powerful that an unshielded ship traveling too close to the ''Executor''{{'s}} wake would be instantly destroyed by the [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]].<ref name="FactFile47" /> The ''Executor'' was outfitted with a Class 2.0 [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] engine for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel<ref name="BTM" /> and a Class 10 [[backup hyperdrive]].<ref name="SOTG2007" /> It had supplies for 300,000 individuals.<ref name="BTM" />

===Armament===
Aside from the Star Dreadnought's unprecedented size, the ''Executor''{{'s}} awesome offensive capabilities set it apart from other warships,<ref name="EGVV" /> bristling with more than 5,000 [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] batteries and [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]].<ref name="SSDDatabank" /> With 2,000 turbolaser batteries, 2,000 heavy turbolaser batteries, 250 [[Concussion missile launcher/Legends|concussion missile batteries]], each armed with thirty [[Assault concussion missile|heavy concussion missiles]], 250 heavy ion cannons, 500 [[Laser/Legends|laser]] [[Point-defense laser cannon/Legends|point-defense cannons]],<ref name="Starship Battles" /> and forty [[Q7 tractor beam projector/Legends|Q7 tractor beam projectors]]<ref name="BTM" /> along its [[City/Legends|city]]-like surface, the ''Executor'' was capable of reducing any [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] surface to slag<ref name="BTM" /> in a matter of [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]].<ref name="GG5" /> The warship's mere presence in an engagement alone was enough to frighten an enemy force into submission.<ref name="EGVV" />

[[File:ExecutorShuttle-ESB.jpg|thumb|right|265px|Darth Vader's shuttle approaches the ''Executor''.]]
While the incredible mass of the ''Executor'' proved an advantage in terms of its firepower and the power of its defensive shields, it likewise proved a disadvantage in keeping the warship supplied&mdash;the ''Executor'' could hold far more resources than the Empire normally had available to provide. More than 100 times as massive as the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer, the ''Executor'' nevertheless boasted quite a formidable complement of support vessels and instruments of ground warfare.<ref name="SOTG2007" />

Standard practice set the ''Executor'' with two [[Fighter wing/Legends|wings]],<ref name="SOTG2007" /> or twelve [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]],<ref name="Brandei">{{CCG|set=Dagobah Limited|cardname=Commander Brandei}}</ref> of varying [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] starfighters, for a total of 144 ships,<ref name="SOTG2007" /> the fighter equivalent of two ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers.<ref name="BTM" /> These two wings primarily comprised [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]], [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bombers]], and [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptors]].<ref name="SOTG" /> By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the starfighter [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] expanded to include [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE/D Defenders]]<ref name="Imperial Ace" /> and [[TIE/ad starfighter]]s.<ref name="XWA" /> The ''Executor'' also routinely hosted [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced/Legends|Darth Vader's TIE Advanced x1]].<ref name="Imperial Ace" /><ref name="SOTE novel" />

Additionally, the ''Executor'' regularly maintained 200 miscellaneous combat and support ships in secondary docking bays,<ref name="NEGVV" /> including [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]],<ref name="FactFile47" /> such as [[Gamma-class ATR-6 assault transport|''Gamma''-class ATR-6 assault transports]] for [[Troop/Legends|troop]] deployment;<ref name="XWA" /> and armed [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]],<ref name="FactFile47" /> such as the [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]],<ref name="SOTG" /> used to transport senior [[Officer/Legends|officers]] and dignitaries.<ref name="FactFile47" />

Likewise, as a standard the ''Executor'' carried a massive [[Army/Legends|army]] that included three [[IM-455 modular garrison|prefabricated garrison bases]];<ref name="EGVV" /> a full [[Corps/Legends|corps]] of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and [[Imperial Army trooper/Legends|Army troopers]];<ref name="AJ12" /> 38,000 ground troops;<ref name="EGVV" /> and hundreds of assault [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] for planetary warfare,<ref name="SOTG2007" /> typically including thirty [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transports]],<ref name="BTM" /> fifty [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transports]],<ref name="NEGVV" /> and [[All Terrain Personal Transport/Legends|All Terrain Personal Transports]], deployed by [[Y-85 Titan dropship/Legends|Y-85 Titan dropships]]<ref name="SWCL" /> and other [[Landing craft/Legends|landing craft]].<ref name="SOTG" /> A small armada of [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]] and [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]] completed the ground arsenal.<ref name="NEGVV" /> In theory, the ''Executor'' could hold far more starships and troops, though such resources were never available.<ref name="SOTG2007" />

===Facilities and accommodations===
[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] had the ''Executor'' specially equipped with a spherical hyperbaric [[Darth Vader's meditation chamber/Legends|meditation chamber]] for his own use within his personal suite. Inside the chamber, which opened by splitting in two, like the gaping maw of some beast, a supermedicated<ref name="FactFile42">{{FactFile|42|MED 1-2|Meditation Chamber}}</ref> high-pressure gas mix allowed Vader to safely rest free of his [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|breathing mask]], aiding his badly damaged [[Lung/Legends|lungs]] in the absorption of [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]], so that his scarred head and face could feel fresh air.<ref name="SWCL" /> The pod's pressurized atmosphere enabled Vader to relax into a meditative state,<ref name="Starships & Vehicles 38">{{StarshipsVehiclesCite|38|Starship & Vehicle Directory}}</ref> providing a sanctuary from the rigors of command.<ref name="Gatefold Poster">{{GalaxyCite|11|Darth Vader Poster}}</ref> While within the chamber, a series of high-bandwidth communications consoles<ref name="SWCL" /> and a large visual display screen<ref name="FactFile42" /> allowed Vader to communicate directly with his commanders on the ''Executor''{{'s}} bridge.<ref name="ESB" /> Just beyond the chamber within the suite rested a [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] transceiver<ref name="Rise and Fall">''[[The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader]]''</ref> [[HoloNet transceiver/Legends|projection pod]] with which Vader could immediately communicate with the [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor]] directly from throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="ESB" />

[[File:MeditationChamber-ESB.png|thumb|left|265px|A special meditation chamber aboard the ''Executor'' allowed Darth Vader to rest free of his breathing mask.]]
The ''Executor''{{'s}} onboard facilities included the central Engineering section, which managed the various systems that kept the titanic vessel running. The Star Dreadnought's powerful engines vibrated through the deckplates of Engineering. Ship security was maintained centrally within a large security office, equipped with various control panels and monitoring stations, including a ring of primary panels positioned in the middle of the office. [[Security camera/Legends|Security cameras]] provided the office with feeds of various portions of the ship. A central [[Droid/Legends|droid]] pool maintained and serviced the ''Executor''{{'s}} many droids. The droid pool's facilities could only be accessed by logging into the system's [[Computer/Legends|computer]] network.<ref name="Murder on the Executor">"[[Murder on the Executor|Murder on the ''Executor'']]"</ref>

Further crew accommodations aboard the ''Executor'' included at least one sparsely furnished, nondescript conference/briefing room near the middle of the ship; dining galleys<ref name="Murder on the Executor" /> and an officers' mess hall in the command tower;<ref name="SWCL" /> at least one recreational facility in the middle of the ship, populated with games, such as [[Dejarik/Legends|dejarik]], programs playing on video screens lining the walls, and dining tables; and an infirmary, with an adjacent reception area, furnished with chairs and [[Couch/Legends|couches]] for waiting patients. The infirmary offered a level of cleanliness surpassing the rest of the ship to meet the needs and desires necessary for the ''Executor''{{'s}} medical staff to perform its duties well.<ref name="Murder on the Executor" />

Located in the levels immediately above the command bridge within the central command structure was a series of suites designed for the ''Executor''{{'s}} [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]]. Adjacent to the suites was a special escape pod for the admiral's specific use.<ref name="SWCL" /> Small cabins and personal quarters accommodated the rest of the ''Executor''{{'s}} crew<ref name="Murder on the Executor" />&mdash;higher-ranking officers were typically afforded solitary quarters within the command structure,<ref name="SWCL" /><ref name="Murder on the Executor" /> while lower-ranking personnel shared cabins with a roommate.<ref name="Murder on the Executor" /> Another area contained the ''Executor''{{'s}} troop quarters.<ref name="Bossk">{{StoryCite|story=The Prize Pelt: The Tale of Bossk|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>

The ''Executor''{{'s}} brig comprised detention<ref name="Scoundrel's Luck">''[[Scoundrel's Luck]]''</ref> and interrogation cells,<ref name="The Will of Darth Vader">''[[Star Wars Adventures: The Will of Darth Vader]]''</ref><ref name="Payback">{{StoryCite|story=Payback: The Tale of Dengar|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> which were roughly four paces in length and large enough to hold at least two individuals.<ref name="Scoundrel's Luck" /> The cells had cots to accommodate slumber<ref name="Payback" /> and ceilings that disappeared into darkness, while the walls had a barren black-gray finish intended to impress upon a captive the hopelessness of the situation.<ref name="Scoundrel's Luck" /> Alternatively, the Super Star Destroyer hosted civilian vessels within its many secondary docking bays, directed by a nearby launch control center. The ''Executor'' charged civilians by the day to keep their vessels docked in its storage bays.<ref name="Bossk" /> A cavernous cargo storage area allowed for another 250,000 metric tons of material in addition to the ''Executor''{{'s}} military complement. Six years' worth of consumables kept the ''Executor''{{'s}} crew members well supplied.<ref name="FactFile47" />

Like all ''Imperial''-class and [[Super-class Star Destroyer|''Super''-class Star Destroyers]], the ''Executor'' was constructed with a special [[Emperor's throne room|throne room]] set aside for exclusive use by the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]. From this throne room, the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] could take control of the Empire in whole and contemplate the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].<ref name="AGSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Vader's on that ship.|Luke Skywalker|audio=VadersOnThatShip.flac|<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>}}
===Design origins===
The ''Executor''{{'s}} origins could be traced back to the final days of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Starship engineer [[Lira Wessex/Legends|Lira Wessex]], daughter of famed [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] engineer [[Walex Blissex/Legends|Walex Blissex]], designed the ''Imperator''-class Star Destroyer, a massive 1,600-meter-long warship with an intimidation factor as great as its firepower,<ref name="Star Destroyer Databank" /> which saw limited use in Republic task forces.<ref name="Clone Wars">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> Following the Republic's [[Declaration of a New Order|transition]] into the Galactic Empire<ref name="Star Destroyer Databank" /> in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> the ''Imperator'', since renamed the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer, became the iconic staple of the Imperial Navy&mdash;a terrifying symbol of the Emperor's might.<ref name="Star Destroyer Databank" /> Recognizing the immense size of the Star Destroyer was largely responsible for its ability to intimidate, Wessex began to design a new warship that would dwarf even the enormous Imperial Star Destroyer.<ref name="GG3" />

The Empire's initial attempt at realizing a larger Star Destroyer class began in the early years of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] with the [[Sarlacc Project]], a top-secret initiative to construct a twelve-[[Kilometer/Legends|kilometer]]-long [[Super Star Destroyer prototype|prototype Super Star Destroyer]]. However, the Empire's project suffered repeated delays<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> and was eventually [[Battle of Byss|sabotaged]] by [[Alderaanian Resistance|insurgent elements]] loyal to [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] before it could be completed.<ref name="Jaws of the Sarlacc">{{DoD|Jaws of the Sarlacc}}</ref> Still, the destroyed prototype would prove to be the forerunner to an even larger Imperial warship.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

[[File:Lira_Wessex.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Starship engineer Lira Wessex, designer of the ''Executor'']]
Wessex's efforts to improve upon the design of the original ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer eventually resulted in the conceptualization of an unprecedented nineteen-kilometer-long Super Star Destroyer,<ref name="GG3" /> the final product of the Sarlacc Project.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> This new starship class was designed to be a terror weapon like the galaxy had never seen.<ref name="SOTG2007" /> With construction authorized by the Emperor,<ref name="GG3" /> the finished product, the first of a new generation of Super Star Destroyers, would serve as the personal flagship of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Lord]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader.<ref name="SOTG2007" />

However, the term "Super Star Destroyer" was by no means an official label. The Imperial Navy initially listed the vessel as a "''Super''-class Star Destroyer" in budget requests to mask the true destructive nature of the warship from the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]. The Imperial Navy even went so far as to incorrectly report the size of the new ship to keep oversight committees from discovering its purpose. Such measures would create naming confusion in attempts at officially classifying the ''Executor'' in the future.<ref name="Starship Battles" />

===Manufacturing contract===
Although Kuat Drive Yards served as the primary manufacturer of the Empire's Star Destroyers, the ''Executor''{{'s}} manufacturing contract was unexpectedly granted to the [[Fondor Shipyards/Legends|Starship Yards of Fondor]]. The Empire demanded total secrecy for the ''Executor'' project, closing off the [[Fondor system/Legends|Fondor system]] to all nonmilitary traffic. No longer able to meet the needs of their most valuable civilian clients, the [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]] executives were enraged. Still, the massive project took up virtually all of Fondor's resources, and they knew better than to test Vader's anger. They also reasoned that if they met the Empire's expectations, they might very well be able to steal future lucrative military contracts from their Kuat competitors.<ref name="EGPM">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref>

In reality, the Empire awarding the ''Executor'' contract to Fondor opened up the KDY [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] for a new project. Having lost the ''Executor'' job, Kuat executives made sure that all future ''Super''-class Star Destroyers would bear their logo,<ref name="EGPM" /> which only further angered Fondor.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> In fact, Kuat would be simultaneously constructing a duplicate Super Star Destroyer for the Empire along with Fondor.<ref name="EGPM" /> The Empire provisionally named both ships "''Executor''" to make it seem as if only one ship was being constructed.<ref name="Bacta War">''[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]''</ref> By attributing all expenses of the [[Lusankya/Legends|sister ship]] to the true ''Executor'', the Empire kept the existence of the second Super Star Destroyer a secret from the galaxy at large.<ref name="SOTG2007" /> Under this ruse, both Kuat and Fondor publicly laid claim to having produced the ''Executor'', Darth Vader's flagship.<ref name="Bacta War" />

===Starkiller's base of operations===
{{Quote|The historical records will claim that the Rebel Alliance was born on Corellia. That ''is'' a documented fact. But the ''truth'' is this: The Rebel Alliance was born somewhere in the Scarl system aboard Darth Vader's personal starship, the ''Executor''.|PROXY's historical analysis|<ref name="TFU comic">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (graphic novel)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' graphic novel]]</ref>}}
The ''Executor'' first began construction at a top-secret [[Scarl|shipyard facility]] in the secluded [[Scarl system/Legends|Scarl system]], located on the restricted Imperial [[Gandeal-Fondor Hyperlane]]&mdash;which the Empire had secretly forged in accordance with the ''Executor'' project&mdash;mere [[Parsec/Legends|parsecs]] from Fondor. Coupled with the Scarl [[Star system/Legends|system's]] anonymity, the ''Executor''{{'s}} Scarl labor force at first consisted entirely of droids, which concealed the Super Star Destroyer's construction quite effectively.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> By [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]],<ref name="TFU">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> thousands of construction droids<ref name="TFU databank">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> continued to labor on the ''Executor'' in complete secrecy,<ref name="Insider 107">{{InsiderCite|107|Ask Lobot}}</ref> and construction had proceeded such that the ship's superstructure was largely completed, and the traditional dagger-shaped hull of a Star Destroyer was recognizable. The command tower had been erected almost in full, with the two shield/sensor globes intact, and the engines were operational. Substantial sections of the hull, including the defined voluminous center, nevertheless remained incomplete, leaving portions of the ''Executor''{{'s}} interior exposed.<ref name="TFU comic" />

[[File:ExecutorScarlSystem-TFU.png|thumb|left|256px|The ''Executor'' undergoes construction in the secluded Scarl system, 3 BBY.]]
During this time, Vader utilized his uncompleted Super Star Destroyer as a training ground and home for a secret dark side apprentice&mdash;[[Galen Marek]], who, unknowing of his true name or identity, operated only under the codename "Starkiller." Vader took great steps to keep the existence of the apprentice hidden from the Emperor, as his taking of an underling was paramount to the betrayal of his own master. The Scarl system provided a location away from the Emperor's [[Spy/Legends|spies]], who perpetually monitored Vader's every move. Aboard the ''Executor'', Vader frequently sparred with the apprentice, training him in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] and other [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetic]] measures of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. The Dark [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] also provided his apprentice with a [[Holodroid/Legends|holodroid]] named [[PROXY]]. Programmed with a variety of highly efficient [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] programs, the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] was similarly capable of engaging the apprentice in what effectively served as combat training, although PROXY, by definition of Vader's programming, truly intended to kill the apprentice each time. Vader planned to eventually overthrow the Emperor and succeed him as ruler of the galaxy with the apprentice at his side.<ref name="TFU" />

[[File:Vader_Starkiller.png|thumb|right|256px|Darth Vader "knights" Starkiller aboard the ''Executor''.]]
While living aboard the uncompleted ''Executor'', Vader and his apprentice occupied a concealed level in the underside of the Super Star Destroyer that had long since been removed from the original floor plans and would go unnoticed by the future crew. The level, while sparse, consisted of an inner sanctum for Vader, a meditation chamber, a droid workshop, sleeping quarters large enough for one, and a hangar deck. Vader's inner sanctum was lined with a wide angular viewport.<ref name="TFU" />

At some point during the next year, Vader dispatched the apprentice on a series of missions designed to test his skills in preparation for deposing the Emperor. To aid the apprentice, Vader secretly assigned the [[Gender/Legends|female]] Imperial [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]] to the ''Executor'' to [[Captain/Legends|captain]] the ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'', the apprentice's starship, under the stipulation that anyone learning of her assignment would mean her [[Death/Legends|death]]. Eclipse had personal quarters on the forty-first deck of the ''Executor''.<ref name="TFU" />

After the apprentice succeeded in his appointed mission, killing three fugitive [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], thus proving his readiness, Vader ordered him to return to the ''Executor'', where together they would finalize their plan to take control of the galaxy. Upon the apprentice's return to the Scarl system, however, Vader discovered that the Emperor's spies had followed him to the ''Executor''{{'s}} hidden location&mdash;the Emperor's personal [[Emperor's fleet|fleet]] of three ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers and a dozen smaller vessels exited hyperspace and surrounded the ''Executor''. Aboard the Super Star Destroyer, the apprentice believed the time had come to strike against the Emperor, but Vader instead [[Shiak|impaled]] the apprentice with his [[Darth Vader's lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], his plan to move against the Emperor a failure. Having learned of Vader's treachery of taking on an apprentice of his own, the Emperor, watching via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] through PROXY, ordered the Dark Lord to kill the apprentice or be killed himself. Vader obeyed by telekinetically throwing the apprentice through one of the ''Executor''{{'s}} transparisteel viewports, out into space.<ref name="TFU" />

[[File:Executortfu.jpg|thumb|left|235px|The Emperor's fleet surrounds the ''Executor''.]]
Vader in fact rescued the apprentice from certain death soon thereafter, treating his grievous injuries over a period of six [[Standard month/Legends|months]], and once more setting him loose upon the galaxy under the guise that he was to organize an armed rebellion against the Empire. With the Emperor distracted with an alliance of rebel dissidents, the apprentice believed, Vader and he would finally strike. In reality, Vader and the Emperor manipulated the apprentice into bringing together the Emperor's greatest [[Politics/Legends|political]] adversaries in one location where they could be eliminated in one fell swoop. On the planet [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]<ref name="TFU" /> in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> the apprentice joined with Imperial Senator Bail Organa and former senators [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] and [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]] to [[Corellian Treaty|discuss the formation]] of an official rebellion against the Empire.<ref name="TFU" /> The ''Executor'' interrupted the clandestine meeting, however. With the Super Star Destroyer looming in the upper [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]<ref name="TFU comic" /> alongside several ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers,<ref name="TFU video game (360)">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', [[Wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]] version</ref> Vader and a [[Squad/Legends|squad]] of stormtroopers seized the three senatorial conspirators, revealing to the apprentice that he had been used all along.<ref name="TFU" />

Vader took the three imprisoned senators to the [[Horuz system/Legends|Horuz system]], the construction site of the incomplete first [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], where the Emperor could execute his enemies personally. In a final [[Battle on Death Star I|confrontation]] with Vader and the Emperor, the apprentice died but liberated his allies nevertheless, freeing them to continue their rebellion. Having become the impetus behind the first significant armed resistance movement against Imperial forces in the galaxy by way of the Emperor's machinations, in a sense the apprentice's efforts staged from the ''Executor'' marked the advent of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="TFU comic" />

===Imperial admirals' plot to sabotage the ''Executor'' project===
{{Quote|Lord Vader advances himself at the expense of me and my fellow officers!&hellip;If Darth Vader's project succeeds, my fellow officers and I lose prestige and power. Rather than see that happen, we've paved the way for your Rebel Alliance to intercede.|Admiral Amise Griff|<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" />}}
As the Death Star project neared completion in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], construction on the ''Executor'' had stalled in turn. The planet-destroying [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] had become the new symbol of Imperial power, and the Death Star was draining much needed resources from the ''Executor'' and other projects.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> Nevertheless, Admiral [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] promised the Super Star Destroyer line's imminent introduction to active service in authoring the Imperial Navy chapter of the ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'', a tactical manual distributed just prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Motti noted the Super Star Destroyer's intended role as the Imperial Navy's primary TIE fighter [[Carrier/Legends|carrier]], troop [[Transport/Legends|transport]], [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]], and [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|planetary bombardment]] platform, declaring also the Empire's ultimate vision to have one Super Star Destroyer per [[Sector/Legends|sector]] as a [[Command ship/Legends|command ship]] for [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial forces]]. The ''Imperial Handbook'' included an image of the still-under-construction ''Executor''.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

Yet following the Death Star's sudden destruction at the Battle of [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]], the ''Executor'' became the Empire's top priority. The nearly completed Super Star Destroyer was hastily towed from the secrecy of the Scarl system to the Starship Yards of Fondor and a living construction crew, who redoubled their efforts to speed up the ''Executor''{{'s}} stalled progress. Although the Empire had [[Imperialization/Legends|nationalized]] Fondor around the time of the Battle of Yavin, it still left the [[Fondor Guild of Starshipwrights]], the planet's ancient rulers, in power to oversee the ''Executor'' project.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

[[File:ExecutorFondor-CSW.png|thumb|right|290px|Construction proceeds at the Starship Yards of Fondor.]]
Construction entered the final stages at Fondor<ref name="Insider 107" /> under the utmost levels of security. A fleet of ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers patrolled Fondor, ordered to destroy any unauthorized civilian craft attempting to gain access to the shipyards. The sheer number of [[Bulk freighter/Legends|bulk freighters]] delivering materials to the shipyards as a result of the ''Executor'' project prompted Fondor to add additional shipping lanes not indicated on standard star charts to accommodate the heavy construction traffic. Admiral [[Amise Griff]] supervised the ''Executor''{{'s}} overall construction at Fondor.<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" />

Following the sudden emergence of the Rebellion in the wake of the Battle of Yavin, work slowdowns and sabotage reached critical levels at Fondor's shipyards. Fearing punishment from the Emperor if the ''Executor'' was not completed according to schedule, the Fondor system's [[Governor/Legends|governor]] loosened security restrictions on the shipyard's workers and extended more generous benefit packages to [[Non-huMan|non-Human]] laborers. Although the governor's measures quelled the unrest, the lighter security only left the ''Executor'' project vulnerable to external saboteurs<ref name="RES">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref>&mdash;namely, a group of five traitorous Imperial admirals.<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" />

After Vader's return to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] following the Imperial disaster at Yavin, the Emperor ordered him to Fondor to personally oversee the final stages of construction of the ''Executor''.<ref name="Missions 18">''[[Star Wars Missions 18: Rogue Squadron to the Rescue]]''</ref> Before reaching Fondor, Vader rendezvoused with the group of Imperial admirals, including Amise Griff, to dictate his decided war policy against the Rebellion. Vader planned to use the ''Executor'' to single-handedly destroy the Alliance, thus taking absolute control of the Imperial war effort, much to the admirals' disgust,<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" /> who viewed the ''Executor''{{'s}} construction as little more than grandstanding.<ref name="NEC" /> They loathed the favor Vader courted from the Emperor, and feared that with the completion of the ''Executor'', they would suffer a great loss of influence and stature.<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" /> Whereas the Death Star had previously eclipsed the Imperial Navy as the Emperor's preferred weapon of terror, the battlestation's destruction at Yavin returned the admirals to their original position of prominence.<ref name="GG3" /> The ''Executor'', however, threatened to once again steal that dominance away and place it solely in Vader's command.<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" />

During the meeting, Vader telekinetically lifted Griff out of his seat in a Force choke in response to the admiral raising an objection against his outlined course against the Rebellion, as well as to intimidate the other admirals into adherence. Vader and Griff in fact staged the entire scene to make it seem as if Griff truly sympathized with the admirals' concerns, when he was actually in league with Vader. The two planned to use the ''Executor'' project to weed out those who sought to undermine Vader in the Emperor's eyes by bringing the project to ruin.<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" />

[[File:ExecutorConstruction-CSW.png|thumb|left|220px|Installation of the ''Executor''{{'s}} massive engines]]
Griff anonymously contacted the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], leaking to them the existence of Vader's secret project at Fondor aimed at the Rebellion's destruction. He explained that he and his fellow Imperial admirals wished to halt Vader's rise in power and therefore had used their influence to keep open a position in the droid maintenance section of the project, which the Alliance could in turn use to their advantage by inserting a spy into that position. [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] volunteered for the [[Mission to Fondor (Galactic Civil War)|mission]], having droid maintenance experience, and, along with the droids [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], he journeyed to the Fondor Shipyards to collect any information he could on Vader's project.<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" /> In addition to Skywalker, the Alliance also dispatched a team of agents to destroy the project.<ref name="FactFile19">{{FactFile|19|VAD 7-12|Darth Vader}}</ref> Only upon arriving did Skywalker discover that Vader's undertaking was nothing less than the largest starship he had ever seen.<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" />

Skywalker's maintenance duties included moving all along the ''Executor'', often repairing droids in zero [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]]. While he kept up the ruse of droid repair, R2-D2 compiled detailed information on the ''Executor''{{'s}} schematics. During his masquerade, Skywalker befriended [[Tanith Shire]], a woman who had also infiltrated the ''Executor'' project in order to steal one of the shipyard's [[Drone barge/Legends|drone barges]].<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" />

With the Rebel spy in place, Vader used the Imperial admirals' ambition to sabotage the ''Executor'' to lure them to Fondor to meet with the spy&mdash;planning to destroy them all at once. After Vader purportedly left the Fondor system to briefly attend to other matters, in actuality remaining on Fondor waiting to strike, Griff and the admirals secretly convened with Skywalker to supply him with explosive weapons necessary to sabotage the ''Executor''. Although Vader's plan to capture the Rebel spy failed when Skywalker sensed the Dark Lord's presence through the Force and escaped the scene, Vader's stormtroopers nevertheless rounded up the traitorous admirals, bringing their scheme to sabotage the ''Executor'' project to an end.<ref name="Darth Vader Strikes" />

Simultaneously, Vader succeeded in uncovering the team of Alliance saboteurs, foiling their sabotage mission as well.<ref name="FactFile19" /> Skywalker eventually returned to the [[Great Temple/Legends|Rebel base]] on Yavin 4<ref name="Traitor's Gambit">"[[Traitor's Gambit]]"</ref>&mdash;the only member of the Alliance team to survive the failed sabotage mission<ref name="FactFile19" />&mdash;with a great deal of information on the ''Executor'' stored within R2-D2, his own mission largely a success.<ref name="Traitor's Gambit" />

===Construction completed===
{{Quote|Gentlemen&hellip;a toast! To celebrate completion of the most powerful new craft in the Imperial fleet!|The ''Executor''{{'s}} first commanders congratulate themselves|<ref name="Trap">"[[It's a Trap]]"</ref>}}
In the interim between the Death Star's destruction and the imminent completion of the ''Executor'', Vader initiated a large-scale, if highly ineffective, [[Yavin blockade|blockade]] of the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]].<ref name="NEC" /> Vader also reassigned Griff away from Fondor to take command of the blockade as the ''Executor'' project neared completion.<ref name="Geonosis">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> Vader did not want to crush the Rebel base immediately, using the blockade as a means to keep the Rebel command in place on Yavin 4 until the ''Executor'' itself was ready to lead a full-scale planetary assault.<ref name="Return of Ben Kenobi">"[[The Return of Ben Kenobi]]"</ref> He planned to use the ''Executor'' as personal retribution for the embarrassment he suffered at Yavin. As the months wore on, however, the blockade situation angered local fleet commanders<ref name="NEC" /> and even Griff himself, who urged Vader to strike.<ref name="Return of Ben Kenobi" /> Consequently, Fondor accelerated the ''Executor''{{'s}} construction.<ref name="NEC" />

Around two months after the Battle of Yavin,<ref name="Star Wars 1">[[Star Wars (2013) 1|''Star Wars'' (2013) 1]]</ref> the ''Executor'' was transferred to the remote [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]], the secret construction site of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] battlestation. Along with a number of ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers, the ''Executor'' patrolled the construction site,<ref name="Star Wars 3">[[Star Wars (2013) 3|''Star Wars'' (2013) 3]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 4">[[Star Wars (2013) 4|''Star Wars'' (2013) 4]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 5">[[Star Wars (2013) 5|''Star Wars'' (2013) 5]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 7">[[Star Wars (2013) 7|''Star Wars'' (2013) 7]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 8">[[Star Wars (2013) 8|''Star Wars'' (2013) 8]]</ref> where the new Death Star's progress fell short of the Emperor's expectations.<ref name="Star Wars 3" /> Still incensed with Vader over his failure at Yavin, the Emperor relieved Vader of his command of the primary Imperial Fleet and reassigned him to administrative duties at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]<ref name="Star Wars 3" /> to ensure the Death Star's continuing progress.<ref name="Star Wars 4" /> Vader's reassignment included relinquishing command of his flagship,<ref name="Star Wars 1" /> the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer<ref name="VUG" /> [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']], to the upstart [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Kell Bircher]].<ref name="Star Wars 1" />

The ''Executor'' played host to the Emperor's eventual arrival at the Endor construction site. The Emperor discovered, much to his disgust, that Vader had appointed [[Birra Seah]],<ref name="Star Wars 7" /> a Kuat Drive Yards systems engineer serving as a liaison to the construction project,<ref name="Star Wars 4" /> as acting [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] in command of the Death Star's construction.<ref name="Star Wars 5" /> However, to save Seah,<ref name="Star Wars 7" /> whom Vader discovered to have a strong [[Force-sensitive/Legends|connection to the Force]],<ref name="Star Wars 4" /> from the Emperor's wrath, he instead surreptitiously placed her in an officer's position aboard the ''Devastator''<ref name="Star Wars 7" /> as his spy to keep tabs on Bircher.<ref name="Star Wars 8" /> From aboard the ''Executor''{{'s}} bridge in the Endor system, Vader remained in regular contact with Seah as she served on the ''Devastator''.<ref name="Star Wars 8" /><ref name="Star Wars 9">[[Star Wars (2013) 9|''Star Wars'' (2013) 9]]</ref> Seah reported to Vader that Bircher captured two Rebels aboard his Star Destroyer, [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] and Luke Skywalker, the latter being of intense interest to the Dark Lord. Vader commanded Seah to detain Skywalker and bring the Rebel immediately to him.<ref name="Star Wars 9" /> Eventually, the ''Executor'' returned to Fondor.<ref name="Trap" />

[[File:ExecutorLaunches-CSW.png|thumb|right|250px|The completed ''Executor'' roars to life.]]
Finally, six months after the Battle of Yavin, the ''Executor'' reached completion<ref name="NEC" /> on schedule.<ref name="FactFile19" /> The first Super Star Destroyer ever constructed, the ''Executor'' represented the most powerful starship in the Imperial Navy inventory<ref name="Trap" /> and, for the matter, the largest and most powerful [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] in the entire galaxy.<ref name="AJ12" /><ref name="FactFile19" /> The ''Executor'', which replaced the Star Destroyer ''Devastator'' as Vader's flagship,<ref name="Slave Ship">''[[Slave Ship]]''</ref> would become the most famous of all the Empire's Star Destroyers,<ref name="Official Figurine Collection 1" /> and held the mantle of Imperial Command Ship.<ref name="Allegiance" /> By time of completion, the ''Executor''{{'s}} official designation was changed from the colloquial Super Star Destroyer to the ''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought. Nevertheless, the term "Super Star Destroyer" stuck and many continued to borrow superlatives from the Clone Wars era and simply classify the ''Executor'' as a ''Super''-class Star Destroyer.<ref name="SSDDatabank" /><ref name="Starship Battles" />

By purely military standards, the completed ''Executor'' was somewhat impractical, since a smaller ship could fulfill its mission duties. Instead, the ''Executor'' served as physical proof of the unlimited resources and might of the Emperor. Indeed, Wessex's design succeeded where the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer had left off&mdash;the ''Executor'' could conquer an enemy through sheer intimidation without even firing a shot,<ref name="EGVV" /> capable of demoralizing a planetary population merely by appearing in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] and even subduing an entire star system.<ref name="FactFile47" />

The ''Executor'' project had taken years to complete,<ref name="Secret Apprentice Databank">{{DB|character|starkiller|Starkiller (Darth Vader's Secret Apprentice)}}</ref> and the incredible cost to fund the construction of such a large warship&mdash;an estimated 1,143,350,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]<ref name="SOTG" />&mdash;had practically bankrupted several star systems.<ref name="IG-88">{{StoryCite|story=Therefore I Am: The Tale of IG-88|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> In fact, years later in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]],<ref name="Darksaber date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of [[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']] to [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]].</ref> Imperial Admiral [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] once remarked that the ''Executor'' alone had practically bankrupted the entire Empire.<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref> The Imperial treatment afforded Fondor during the ''Executor''{{'s}} construction&mdash;namely locking out all civilian traffic from the Fondor system and awarding subsequent Super Star Destroyer contracts to their [[Kuati/Legends|Kuati]] competitors&mdash;would erode support for the Emperor at Fondor and eventually lead to the Empire losing the planet to the Rebellion, reportedly with inside help, in the years following.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

The ''Executor''{{'s}} completion paved the way for the introduction of the new warship line. Three Super Star Destroyers would enter service in the three years following, with several more under construction.<ref name="EGVV" /> At the same time that Fondor completed work on the ''Executor'', Kuat Drive Yards likewise finished the ''Executor''{{'s}} sister ship.<ref name="SOTG2007" /> Rechristened the ''Lusankya'', the duplicate Super Star Destroyer was interred on Coruscant as the Emperor's private escape vessel,<ref name="EGPM" /> while Vader pressed the ''Executor'' into immediate active military service.<ref name="Trap" />

===Maiden voyage and approach to Yavin 4===
{{Quote|The ''Executor'' performed magnificently, Lord Vader! The destruction is complete!''"<br />"''No, Admiral&hellip;it is just beginning!|The ''Executor''{{'s}} [[Unidentified Imperial admiral (Griff's successor)|interim admiral]] and Darth Vader, following the destruction of Laakteen Depot|<ref name="Trap" />}}
Vader's impatience barely allowed surrounding [[Cargo tug/Legends|space tugs]] and [[Freighter/Legends|equipment barges]] time to scatter out of the way as the finished ''Executor'' blasted out of the Fondor Shipyards. Vader ordered his commanders to set course for the nearest Rebel installation to christen his new warship by testing its destructive power. The ''Executor''{{'s}} maiden voyage saw it [[Destruction of Laakteen Depot|annihilate]] the Rebel outpost at [[Laakteen Depot]] with little resistance, a stronghold the Rebellion had fought nearly a year to win.<ref name="Trap" /> While a minor skirmish, the ''Executor''{{'s}} destruction of Laakteen Depot served both a military and political purpose, demonstrating to the Rebel Alliance and the galaxy that the Rebellion's victory over the Death Star was by pure chance and that the new Super Star Destroyer, of which there would be many more, was unstoppable.<ref name="SSDDatabank" /> With the outpost left a smoldering ruin, the ''Executor'' continued on toward the Rebel base on Yavin 4.<ref name="Trap" />

[[File:Laakteen-CSW.png|thumb|left|255px|The ''Executor'' annihilates Laakteen Depot.]]
En route to Yavin 4, the ''Executor'' soon [[Battle of Skorrupon (Galactic Civil War)|fell under attack]] at the planet [[Skorrupon/Legends|Skorrupon]] by a Rebel task force<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> consisting of an [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] and two [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvettes]] trying to slow the Super Star Destroyer's advance. Rather than taking immediate action against the attackers, Vader ordered the ''Executor'' to stand down momentarily, allowing the Rebel ships a strafing run across the ''Executor''{{'s}} prow, which inflicted minimal damage against its shields. The ''Executor''{{'s}} [[Unidentified Imperial admiral (Griff's successor)|acting admiral]] at first worried at Vader's delay, but the Dark Lord was simply toying with his ship's prey. After a moment longer, the ''Executor'' easily destroyed the three Rebel ships. Vader acknowledged that his hesitation was to allow the Rebels time to report back to the Rebel base the ''Executor''{{'s}} advance toward Yavin 4, before ordering the Super Star Destroyer onward with no delay.<ref name="Doom Mission" />

Knowing the ''Executor'' inexorably neared Yavin 4, the situation at the Rebel base turned desperate. The ''Executor'' threatened to wipe out the Rebellion's top starfighter pilots, including Luke Skywalker and a core group that would eventually form the elite [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], if the base was destroyed.<ref name="NEC" /> Alliance [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] had no choice but to therefore order a full [[Evacuation of Yavin|evacuation of the base]] despite the Imperial blockade waiting to ensnare the fleeing Rebel transports,<ref name="Race for Survival">"[[Race for Survival]]"</ref> but he still held out hope for one last remaining chance of stopping the ''Executor''{{'s}} approach.<ref name="Doom Mission" />

[[File:ExecutorCorvettes-CSW.png|thumb|right|220px|The ''Executor'' left behind a wake of Rebel destruction en route to Yavin 4.]]
Using the detailed information Skywalker collected during his spy mission of the uncompleted ''Executor'' at Fondor, Dodonna and the Rebellion previously discovered several possible exploitable weaknesses in the Super Star Destroyer. First, however, they would need to break through the ''Executor''{{'s}} powerful deflector shields, a near impossible task only an entire fleet would likely be able to accomplish&mdash;resources the Rebellion certainly did not have at their disposal.<ref name="The Power Gem">"[[The Power Gem]]"</ref> Instead, they planned to use a [[power gem]]&mdash;a rare [[Meteorite/Legends|meteorite]] particle once used by the [[Iridium Pirates/Legends|Pirates of Iridium]] during the days of the Old Republic that could disable any starship's energy shields&mdash;to knock out the ''Executor''{{'s}} own shielding system and inflict enough damage to stop the approaching warship. The inherent risk was that the gem's power was rapidly deteriorating and time was of the essence. If the power gem failed to disable the Super Star Destroyer's shields, it would be a suicide mission, and the ''Executor'' would be clear to destroy the Rebel base.<ref name="Doom Mission" />

Both Skywalker and [[Vrad Dodonna]], Jan Dodonna's son, volunteered for the mission. The younger Dodonna had participated in the Rebellion's previous failed attack on the ''Executor'' at Skorrupon, except the monstrous Super Star Destroyer had broken the man's spirit entirely and had sent him running back to Yavin 4 with deliberate, personally inflicted damage to his [[Vrad Dodonna's scout ship|scout ship]] to mask his cowardice. Completely disillusioned with the Rebel Alliance, Dodonna planned to sabotage the mission to stop the ''Executor'' and use the power gem to bargain with the Empire for his life.<ref name="Doom Mission" />

===Stopped by Rebel power gem attack===
{{Quote|I&mdash;It's remarkable that with time for only one brief shot&hellip;the Rebels were able to hit one of our few vulnerable spots, Lord Vader!''"<br />"''Is it, Admiral? Those who served on the Death Star might disagree&hellip;if they were still alive!|The ''Executor''{{'s}} admiral and Darth Vader|<ref name="Doom Mission" />}}
The ''Executor'' encountered Skywalker and Dodonna in their special [[power-gem attack ship]] in the [[Feswe Corridor]], an uninhabited star system filled with densely packed, tumbling [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]],<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> the cover of which provided a perfect spot for the [[Skirmish in the Feswe Corridor|Rebel attack]]. The ''Executor''{{'s}} [[Unidentified Imperial admiral (Executor)|second acting admiral]] derided the attack as foolhardy, believing a single small vessel could do no harm, especially since the Rebels' capital ships had so easily been defeated previously at Skorrupon. Vader, however, remembered how a single starfighter had destroyed the Death Star. Taking no chances, he ordered the admiral to maintain full shields and for the [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] to open fire on the Rebel craft.<ref name="Doom Mission" />

[[File:ExecutorVrad-CSW.png|thumb|left|250px|Vrad Dodonna's power-gem attack ship fails to stop the ''Executor''.]]
Dodonna wildly maneuvered the vessel away from the ''Executor'' but purposely vectored close enough for the power gem to nearly penetrate the Super Star Destroyer's shields, hoping the Empire would detect the anomaly, which would then allow him to purchase his own safety. Vader instantly realized that the Rebel attack ship was indeed equipped with such a power gem, but the craft had come close enough to the ''Executor'' that Vader had also sensed the Force in one of the ship's pilots. Believing the sensation to be emanating from none other than his own son, Luke Skywalker, Vader ordered the ''Executor'' to reverse its course heading away from Yavin 4 to pursue the Rebel craft, which had disappeared from sight.<ref name="Doom Mission" />

Once the Rebel ship reappeared, after landing on a nearby [[Planetoid/Legends|planetoid]] where Dodonna expelled Skywalker from the craft, the ''Executor'' continued pursuit. The primary acting admiral, concerned that the ''Executor''{{'s}} battle schedule did not allow for such a deviation from its course toward Yavin 4, voiced his concerns to Vader, but the Dark Lord silenced his commander by momentarily closing his windpipe with the Force. Vader considered a chance at capturing Skywalker worth delaying the attack on the Rebel base. He ordered the ''Executor'' to capture the Rebel ship by [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] in order to take Skywalker alive.<ref name="Doom Mission" />

[[File:FalconAttacksExecutor-CSW.png|thumb|right|270px|The ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} attack renders the ''Executor'' temporarily unable to continue its approach to Yavin 4.]]
However, Vader grew concerned when he could no longer sense the presence of the being whom he believed to be Skywalker aboard the Rebel ship, since Skywalker had indeed disembarked. Only when Dodonna suddenly changed course to attack the ''Executor'' head on in a suicide maneuver as part of a change of heart did Vader realize he had indeed lost Skywalker. With shields transferred fully forward, the ''Executor'' suffered little damage as the Rebel craft slammed into the Super Star Destroyer at full force. Although the power gem's strength had weakened enough to have no effect on the ''Executor'', setting the shields forward left the ''Executor''{{'s}} entire aft section unshielded and vulnerable. [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and Skywalker in the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] took advantage of the momentary lapse by firing off one brief shot at the ''Executor''{{'s}} engines, disabling its gyro-control system. Once more drawing a parallel to the Death Star's destruction, Vader saw nothing extraordinary in that the Rebels succeeded in hitting one of the few vulnerable spots on the ''Executor'' with a single shot.<ref name="Doom Mission" />

The attack left the ''Executor'' temporarily unable to turn and resume its approach to Yavin 4. Having successfully slowed the ''Executor'', the Rebellion bought enough time to complete the evacuation of Yavin Base. Vader allowed responsibility to subsequently fall upon the shoulders of Griff, in charge of the blockade, to stop the Rebels fleeing from Yavin 4 until the ''Executor'' could complete repairs. Griff hoped to reap the full accolades of the opportunity placed before him by crushing the Rebellion himself, not Vader.<ref name="Doom Mission" /> Meanwhile, the ''Executor'' fell back from the Feswe Corridor to the nearby planet [[Toprawa/Legends|Toprawa]] for repairs.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

===Race to destroy the Rebel Fleet===
{{Quote|Three of our own cruisers! Dropping out of hyperspace right into us, Lord Vader!|''Executor'' [[Unidentified Imperial commander (Executor, Feswe)|commander]]|<ref name="Race for Survival" />}}
Vader soon learned, however, that the Rebels had indeed evacuated Yavin 4, though he still trusted Griff, in charge of the Imperial blockade, to stop the escaping [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Fleet]] while the ''Executor'' continued repairs at Toprawa. To help effect the fleet's escape, the Rebels orchestrated a three-pronged simultaneous attack at different points along the Imperial blockade, including a [[Battle of the Vallusk Cluster|diversionary strike]] in the [[Vallusk Cluster/Legends|Vallusk Cluster]], which succeeded in drawing enough of the blockade away to open up a small hole leading to a hyperspace escape corridor. Griff quickly figured out that the Rebel strikes were designed to do nothing more than divert his attention from their true course, and he ordered the three ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers under his command to make all haste to cut off the Rebel Fleet, but he refrained from informing Vader and the ''Executor'' of the Rebels' actions or location.<ref name="Race for Survival" />

[[File:ExecutorFeswe-CSW.png|thumb|left|200px|Approaching the fleeing Rebel Fleet]]
What Griff failed to realize was that the Rebels had discovered an alternate escape corridor away from Griff's waiting Star Destroyers,<ref name="Race for Survival" /> albeit an extremely dangerous one that passed perilously close to the erupting stellar flares of the unstable [[Feswe Prime|red giant star]] of the [[Feswe Prime system/Legends|Feswe Prime system]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> Although the ''Executor''{{'s}} admiral feared that Griff would steal the glory away from the ''Executor'' by destroying the Rebels himself, Vader carefully bided his time, knowing that if Griff hounded the Rebel Fleet hard enough, Luke Skywalker would eventually use the Force to try and help his allies escape, which Vader would be able to sense. When Vader did, the ''Executor'' would arrive to annihilate the Rebel Fleet.<ref name="Race for Survival" />

The ''Executor''{{'s}} admiral's constant whining about Griff soon exhausted Vader, and the Dark Lord executed his ship's commander by choking him to death. After several hours, the ''Executor'' finally completed repairs, although Vader refrained from rushing his ship into action. He patiently continued to wait for Skywalker's Force signature to reveal the Rebel Fleet's location.<ref name="Race for Survival" />

Vader's instincts proved correct when Skywalker began using the Force to sense when the Feswe Prime sun's stellar flares would erupt, safely guiding elements of the Rebel Fleet past the danger during intermittent lulls. Detecting Skywalker's tapping into the Force, Vader immediately ordered the ''Executor'' to make for the Rebel Fleet's escape route past the unstable sun. Meanwhile, having learned that the ''Executor''{{'s}} damage had been repaired and that the Rebel Fleet had begun escaping into hyperspace at the alternate escape corridor at Feswe Prime, Griff desperately ordered his three Star Destroyers to execute a quick hyperspace [[Precision hyperspace jump|micro-jump]], hoping to bring his ships out on the far side of the unstable sun where they would intercept the remainder of the Rebel Fleet. It would be a race to the finish between the ''Executor'' and Griff's Star Destroyers to see which ships arrived first to wipe out the Rebel Fleet.<ref name="Race for Survival" />

[[File:GriffMeetsExecutor-CSW.png|thumb|right|290px|Griff's Star Destroyers collide with the ''Executor''{{'s}} shields.]]
The ''Executor'' exited hyperspace on the far side of the unstable sun first, ahead of Griff, just as the final element of the Rebel Fleet approached its hyperspace jump point. As the ''Executor'' moved around the sun, the Rebel Fleet's approach brought its ships right into the ''Executor''{{'s}} path. With still no sign of Griff, Vader ordered the ''Executor'' to open fire with all guns on the Rebel Fleet, but the Super Star Destroyer never had the chance. At that moment, Griff's three Star Destroyers suddenly emerged from hyperspace right on top of the ''Executor''. Although the ''Executor''{{'s}} powerful shields protected the ship from sustaining any significant damage, Griff and his Star Destroyers were instantly obliterated in the collision. The Star Destroyers' inaccurate hyperspace jump stopped the ''Executor''{{'s}} pursuit cold, allowing the last remnants of the Rebel Fleet to escape safely into hyperspace. Once more, Vader and the ''Executor'' had failed to capture Luke Skywalker, but the Dark Lord vowed that the time would come when he would confront his son.<ref name="Race for Survival" />

Following the Rebels' evacuation from Yavin, Vader discussed the Empire's misfortunes with the Emperor via his private [[Holoprojection chamber|holographic chamber]] aboard the ''Executor'', ensuring his master that their destiny would be fulfilled.<ref name="RS III: Rebel Strike">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref> Around this time, Vader's personal chambers aboard the ''Executor'' continued to play host to further holographic communications between Vader and the Emperor regarding the Imperial quest for dominion. The Dark Lords reassured themselves of the Rebellion's impending doom despite the defection of Imperial pilot [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]] to the Rebellion and his theft of certain Imperial intelligence, which resulted in the escape of Rebel [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] on the planet [[Ralltiir/Legends|Ralltiir]].<ref name="RS III: Rebel Strike" />

Shortly after taking possession of the ''Executor'', Vader conducted a holographic conference from the bridge of his Super Star Destroyer with the Emperor and the [[Dark Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]], the secret head of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] crime syndicate, in the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]] on Coruscant to discuss Xizor's plan to [[Bounty Hunter Wars|destroy]] the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]]. The success of the plan, which splintered the Guild into disparate factions, allowed Vader to frequently hire these free-agent [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] in the future for his own ends.<ref name="Slave Ship" />

===Formation of Death Squadron===
{{Quote|&hellip;with the destruction of the Death Star, the Empire's need for an even greater show of force became not a return to the days of the great fleets, but the dawning of the day of the greatest fleet.|From the writings of Rebel Alliance historian Voren Na'al|<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>}}
The destruction of the Death Star forced the Empire to consider the Rebellion a far greater threat than ever before imagined. The Emperor offered Vader a free hand in hunting down the elusive Rebel High Command, which had disappeared since their escape at Yavin, and the ''Executor'' was the Emperor's gift to Vader to achieve that end. Vader took this liberty to call together a fleet of his favored and, indeed, some of the best, Star Destroyers of the Imperial Navy to assist him in his hunt.<ref name="GG3" /> They primarily included the ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyers [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']] and ''[[Stalker/Legends|Stalker]]'',<ref name="BTM" /> and the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyers [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']],<ref name="GG3" /> [[Conquest (Imperial-class)/Legends|''Conquest'']], [[Emancipator|''Accuser'']] and [[Rebel Dream|''Tyrant'']],<ref name="BTM" /> though they were all merely ornamental compared to the might of the ''Executor''.<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:SW_Executor_01.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Death Squadron marked the most powerful fleet assembled in galactic history.]]
The code-named Imperial [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], elements of which had originally been formed under Griff during his command of the ''Executor'' prior to his death and failure to stop the Rebel evacuation from Yavin 4, represented the most powerful fleet of warships ever assembled in the history of the galaxy. Accordingly enough, the fleet epitomized typical Imperial overkill and inefficiency, much like the ''Executor'' itself.<ref name="GG3" /> Death Squadron's official insignia featured an ''Executor''-class Super Star Destroyer against the backdrop of the Imperial emblem.<ref name="Death Squadron logo">{{WebCite|url=http://battlefrontmobile.thqwireless.com/images/squadron/squadlogo19.gif|text=StarWars BattleFront Mobile Squadron|work=[[Star Wars Battlefront: Mobile Squadrons]] [http://battlefrontmobile.thqwireless.com/index_english.jsp Official Website]|nobackup=1}}</ref>

Death Squadron's formation became a public event, for the Emperor no longer considered it necessary to keep the threat of the Rebellion a secret.<ref name="GG3" /> A reminder to the galaxy of the Empire's power,<ref name="BTM" /> Death Squadron had but one goal: locate the Rebel Alliance and destroy it. Still, Vader had a more specific goal in mind&mdash;namely, the capture of Luke Skywalker.<ref name="GG3" />

Following Death Squadron's formation, [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Imperial Advisor]] [[Ars Dangor/Legends|Ars Dangor]] issued a [[Holomessage/Legends|holomessage]] to the Imperial Military hierarchy and the Empire's [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moffs]] on behalf of the Emperor, announcing the fleet's creation and the ''Executor''{{'s}} mission to hunt down the Alliance High Command. Dangor stressed that those receiving the message were to do whatever Vader and the ''Executor'' required in the completion of their task.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook, Second Edition" />

===Shelkonwa blockade===
{{Quote|I guess you ground-thumpers don't need to keep up with Fleet news. The ''Executor'' just happens to be the brand-new flagship of the Lord Darth Vader.|Renegade Imperial stormtrooper Joak Quiller|<ref name="Allegiance" />}}
In 0 ABY,<ref name="TERC" /> after the Rebels' evacuation of Yavin 4, the ''Executor'' returned Vader to Coruscant, seat of power for the Empire.<ref name="Allegiance" />

The ''Executor'' later continued to orbit the Imperial [[Capital/Legends|capital]] while Vader conducted archival research concerning the whereabouts of Luke Skywalker. Another opportunity for Vader to capture his son came in the form of a message Chief Administrator [[Vilim Disra]] of the remote [[Shelsha sector/Legends|Shelsha sector]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] sent to Vader on Imperial Center, informing him that the fugitive Princess [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] was present on the planet [[Shelkonwa]], the sector capital. Knowing Organa was the key to locating Skywalker, Vader and the ''Executor'' set course for Shelkonwa.<ref name="Allegiance" />

Under commanding officer Admiral [[Bentro]], the ''Executor'' initiated a [[Skirmish on Shelkonwa|lockdown of Shelkonwa]], disallowing any ships landing clearance at the [[Shelkonwa governor's palace|palace]] of sector Governor [[Barshnis Choard]] within [[Makrin City]], the planetary capital, while Vader's elite personal stormtrooper contingent, the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], conducted a search for Organa. During the blockade, the ''Executor'' intercepted an approaching [[Suwantek Systems]] [[TL-1800 transport|TL-1800 freighter]], the ''[[Melnor Spear]]'', carrying five renegade Imperial stormtroopers&mdash;the self-titled [[Hand of Judgment]]&mdash;as well as the Rebels Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, and the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], the latter of whom had come to Shelkonwa to extract Organa from Imperial danger. After the ''Melnor Spear'' provided a legitimate clearance code for passage under a fake [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder code]], masking its true identity as an [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] vessel commandeered by the rogue stormtroopers, the ''Executor'' permitted the ship to land.<ref name="Allegiance" />

[[File:Executor_09_crop.jpg|thumb|right|270px|The ''Executor''{{'s}} very presence was enough to frighten an entire star system into subjugation.]]
The ''Executor'' just as soon intercepted a second vessel, a [[Z-10 Seeker-class scout ship|Z-10 Seeker]] piloted by none other than the young [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]], a rival of Vader's for the Emperor's favor, who had come to Shelkonwa to administer her brand of Imperial justice to the traitorous Barshnis Choard. Much to the befuddlement of the ''Executor''{{'s}} [[Unidentified Executor controller|controller]], Jade identified herself as the Emperor's Hand, demanding to see Vader himself aboard the flagship, hoping to ensure Vader's presence on Shelkonwa didn't interfere with her mission. After a few moments, Vader personally granted her permission to come aboard, and the ''Executor''{{'s}} [[Unidentified Imperial captain (Executor, Shelkonwa)|captain]] directed her to his personal hangar bay. Vader met with Jade in a small conference room, quickly coming to the rash assumption that she intended to capture Leia Organa as part of her own mission. The Dark Lord ignited his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], fully determined to destroy her rather than allowing her to ruin his chance at seizing Organa and thus destroying the opportunity to capture Luke Skywalker. But after realizing that Jade's target was in fact Choard and not Organa, Vader relaxed, recognized her duty to deal with Choard, and left her with the strict caveat not to get in his way.<ref name="Allegiance" />

During Vader's meeting with Jade, the ''Executor'' intercepted yet a third vessel, the freighter ''[[Happer's Way]]'', a stolen ship piloted by the [[BloodScar]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Caaldra]], carrying a cargo of fifty likewise stolen Imperial AT-STs. In league with Choard, Caaldra was delivering the walkers to Shelkonwa to facilitate the independence of the Shelsha sector from Imperial authority for his group's own end. Once Jade returned to her ship, she noted the freighter ahead of her veering off the course the ''Executor'' had allowed for incoming vessels and soon recognized the freighter for who and what it was. Learning from the ''Executor''{{'s}} [[Controller/Legends|controller]] that the Super Star Destroyer had granted the freighter special permission to land at the governor's palace, Jade exercised her authority as Emperor's Hand to order Bentro to redirect the ''Happer's Way'' back to its original landing zone, to which the ''Executor'' complied. Bentro asked whether she required ground troops or air support from the ''Executor'', but she declined, not wanting to elbow Vader twice in the same day, to the quiet relief of the admiral. Jade would handle Choard and Caaldra herself.<ref name="Allegiance" />

The three parties the ''Executor'' allowed into Shelkonwa converged upon one another within Makrin City. The Rebels rescued Organa from Imperial capture and Jade eliminated Caaldra. Vader and the 501st Legion stormed upon the governor's palace and arrested Choard, before taking him aboard the ''Executor'' for prisoner transfer to Coruscant. Jade ordered the ''Executor'' to allow clearance for the five stormtroopers of the Hand of Judgment safe passage off Shelkonwa, protecting their identities as fugitives of the Empire, though she did not realize that the stormtroopers were secretly transporting the Rebels from Shelkonwa as well.
